column3: the theorem the README links (a contract equation's lean_theorem names it), or N/A / open with the reason
quicksort returns a sorted permutation of its input (lists over any linear order)
population and sample variance are >= 0 (over the reals; see docs/lean-proofs.md for the other four)
transposing twice returns the matrix (row-major storage, entries moved, never computed)
composite Simpson with an even panel count is exact on every cubic (over the reals)
its claims (roundtrip within 1e-10, Parseval) are floating-point tolerances; over the reals they are textbook DFT facts, not facts about this code
the integer recurrences are pinned by golden vectors and Kani, and uniformity is a statistical property, not a theorem
the error bound is a probabilistic statement about a pseudo-random stream; it is falsified by tests, not proved
root finders: convergence needs analysis beyond this issue (GH-5 did sort, transpose, variance, Simpson)
golden section and Newton: convergence needs analysis beyond this issue
Dijkstra, BFS, DFS, Kruskal: correctness proofs are not written yet
